description: We are AstroCadets, Software Engineering students from COMSATS Islamabad. We are building a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer - an interactive web app where kids train like astronauts through packing, spacecraft repair, and Moon landing missions using NASA facts and images. Lead skills: React, TypeScript, Web Development. Looking for teammates for design, research/content, and presentation/video.
summary:
AstroCadets is an interactive educational application that helps students explore the engineering trade-offs behind lunar and Martian outposts. Students receive 100 fictional training credits, choose NASA-documented technology challenges, and discover how their decisions connect to other unresolved engineering needs.

The application combines a Mission Trainer, a Decision Atlas, an illustrative Earth–Moon–Mars journey, and a private Mission Notebook. Its evidence layer uses NASA’s 2025 Architecture-Driven Technology Gaps workbook, with traceable source references.

AstroCadets addresses the Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer challenge by making resource allocation and systems thinking approachable through interactive choices. Students learn that addressing one engineering problem does not automatically resolve every connected dependency. NASA evidence is clearly distinguished from fictional classroom mechanics.
details:
THE PROBLEM

Future lunar and Martian outposts involve interconnected engineering challenges. Students need opportunities to explore these connections and understand why limited resources require careful choices.

OUR SOLUTION

AstroCadets is a browser-based educational mission trainer. Students choose a lunar or Mars scenario and allocate 100 fictional training credits to NASA-documented technology challenges. Each challenge includes a plain-language learning summary and expandable source evidence.

After students select their plan, the application generates a mission debrief. It treats the selected technology gaps as hypothetically addressed, removes only those gaps from its loaded relationship graph, and identifies other gaps still connected to the affected architecture nodes. This demonstrates how engineering dependencies can remain after an individual problem is addressed.

MAIN EXPERIENCES

• Mission Trainer: destination selection, searchable challenge cards, system filters, a fictional budget, and an interactive debrief.

• Decision Atlas: explore technology gaps and their explicit architecture references, compare gaps, inspect remaining dependencies, and view source provenance.

• 3D Mission Context: an illustrative Earth–Moon–Mars journey with equivalent text descriptions when 3D is unavailable.

• Mission Notebook: save and revisit training plans through an anonymous browser session without creating an account.

NASA DATA

The application uses a snapshot of NASA’s 2025 Architecture-Driven Technology Gaps workbook, part of Architecture Definition Document Revision C. The imported dataset contains 57 technology gaps, 201 explicit use-case/function nodes, and 308 mappings. Source references identify the relevant workbook records.

CREATIVITY AND EDUCATIONAL BENEFIT

AstroCadets connects an approachable resource-allocation activity to traceable NASA engineering evidence. Its intended learning outcome is systems thinking: students compare choices and discover why addressing one need may leave other dependencies unresolved.

TOOLS AND IMPLEMENTATION

The application uses React, TypeScript, Vite, an Express API, and Three.js for the illustrative 3D experience. It supports SQLite for local deployment and PostgreSQL for persistent hosted storage. The live application is deployed on Vercel.

DESIGN CONSIDERATIONS AND LIMITATIONS

We considered readability, responsive layouts, keyboard access, source transparency, anonymous saved plans, and alternatives to 3D content.

Training budgets, costs, scenarios, and 3D placements are fictional educational mechanics. They are not NASA engineering costs or mission plans. A node with no remaining loaded mapping is not necessarily safe, complete, or flight-ready. The application explores dependencies within its imported dataset and does not calculate mission-success probabilities.
